demoNotice: Illustrative prototype policies only. Verify all disposal instructions against the relevant municipality's rules before real-world use.

Organic.label: Organic waste
Organic.advice: Place food scraps and garden waste in the locally designated wet/organic-waste container. Keep plastic packaging out.

Plastic.label: Plastic
Plastic.advice: Empty and, where locally accepted, rinse the item. Place it in the designated dry-recyclables stream; local acceptance varies by resin and condition.

Paper & cardboard.label: Paper & cardboard
Paper & cardboard.advice: Keep paper dry and reasonably clean. Greasy or food-contaminated paper may not be accepted in paper recycling.

Glass.label: Glass
Glass.advice: Follow local glass collection rules. Wrap broken glass securely and label it to reduce injury risk.

Metal.label: Metal
Metal.advice: Empty the item and use the locally designated metal-recycling stream if accepted.

E-waste.label: Electronic waste
E-waste.advice: Do not place electronics or batteries in ordinary household waste. Use an authorized e-waste or battery collection channel and request municipal guidance.

Potentially hazardous.label: Potentially hazardous waste
Potentially hazardous.advice: Do not mix this item with ordinary waste. Avoid opening or handling leaking contents and contact the appropriate municipal or specialist collection service.

Textile.label: Textile waste
Textile.advice: Reuse or donate clean, usable textiles where possible. Check local textile collection options for damaged material.

Mixed / unknown.label: Mixed or unidentified waste
Mixed / unknown.advice: Separate visible materials if safe to do so. If the material is unclear or potentially hazardous, request a human review before disposal.
